title: Luttinger Liquid Behavior in a Single-Layer Nickelate La1.4Sr0.6NiO4
authors: Yinqi Hu, Yidian Li, Xian Du, Wenxuan Zhao, Kaiyi Zhai, Senyao Zhang, Jiawei Shao, Mingxin Mao, Houke Chen, Jieyi Liu, Donghui Lu, Makoto Hashimoto, Fangyuan Zhu, Zhengtai Liu, Dawei Shen, Yaobo Huang, Zhongkai Liu, D. Prabhakaran, Yanpeng Qi, Yilin Wang, Yulin Chen, Lexian Yang
abstract: The discovery of high-temperature superconductivity in bilayer and trilayer nickelates has spurred intense interest in the Ruddlesden-Popper nickelates; yet the fundamental properties of the NiO2 layer remain obscured by interlayer coupling. It is therefore imperative to investigate the electronic properties of their single-layer counterpart to isolate the intrinsic physics of the NiO layer. In this work, we present a systematic study of the single-layer nickelate La1.4Sr0.6NiO4 using high-resolution angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) and theoretical calculations. We reveal strong electron correlation effects, manifested by high-energy kinks in band dispersions and a pronounced orbital-dependent band renormalization. Interestingly, we observe a quasi-one-dimensional electronic structure characterized by straight Fermi surface sheets along the diagonal momentum directions. Such square Fermi surface topology facilitates non-Fermi liquid behavior consistent with the Luttinger liquid model, as evidenced by the power-law spectral function, robust temperature scaling, and the observation of spin-charge separation. Our results therefore not only unveil an exotic Luttinger liquid behavior emerging from the unexpected dimensional reduction in an intrinsically quasi-two-dimensional nickelate but also provide a new perspective for understanding the intriguing physics in multilayer nickelates.
summary: This work investigates the single-layer nickelate $	ext{La}_{1.4}	ext{Sr}_{0.6}	ext{NiO}_4$ to probe its intrinsic electronic properties. Using ARPES and advanced theory, the authors reveal that the material exhibits quasi-1D electronic behavior, leading to Luttinger liquid physics. This finding offers a crucial, simplified model for understanding the complex correlation physics in higher-dimensional superconducting nickelates.
main_problem: To isolate and understand the intrinsic electronic physics of the single-layer $	ext{NiO}_2$ layer in nickelates, separating it from complications arising from interlayer coupling in multi-layer superconductors.
main_result: The single-layer nickelate exhibits quasi-one-dimensional electronic structure leading to non-Fermi liquid behavior consistent with the Luttinger liquid model, evidenced by power-law spectral functions and spin-charge separation.
method: The study combines high-resolution Angle-Resolved Photoemission Spectroscopy (ARPES) measurements with advanced theoretical calculations like DFT+DMFT.
model_or_system: The physical system is the single-layer nickelate $	ext{La}_{1.4}	ext{Sr}_{0.6}	ext{NiO}_4$. The theoretical framework involves modeling strong electron correlations using Hubbard-type Hamiltonians and calculating the electron self-energy.
key_observables: Band dispersions, Fermi surface topology (straight segments), power-law spectral function, spin-charge separation signatures, and the Luttinger liquid anomalous exponent ($\alpha$).
important_parameters: Doping level ($x=0.6$), temperature range (21 K to 185 K), and the correlation strength parameterized by $U$ and $J_H$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the quasi-1D nature of the Fermi surface dictates the low-energy physics, allowing for a Luttinger liquid description.
figures_summary: Figures detail ARPES results showing parallel line segments for the Fermi surface, band dispersions exhibiting kinks, and plots demonstrating the temperature dependence consistent with LL scaling.
paper_structure: The paper systematically presents ARPES data to establish the quasi-1D nature of the electronic structure, uses theoretical calculations (DFT+DMFT) to model correlation effects, and finally analyzes the temperature and doping dependence to confirm Luttinger liquid behavior.
why_interesting: The observation of Luttinger liquid physics in a quasi-2D cuprate/nickelate platform provides a strong analogy to 1D quantum systems, which is highly relevant for understanding emergent quantum phases in strongly correlated materials.
